to the repository root; every release.yml in this library expects both
there by these names.
WHAT TO CHANGE
1. `release-type` under `packages`. This is the only field that must
change. It decides which files release-please rewrites the version
into. Valid values for the languages in this library:
go      simple    (release-please will not edit go.mod; see below)
python  python    (pyproject.toml, __init__.py, setup.py)
rust    rust      (Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock)
node    node      (package.json and the lock file)
java    maven     (every pom.xml in the reactor)
cmake   simple    (plus extra-files, below)
zig     simple    (plus extra-files, below)
`simple` means release-please tags and writes the changelog but edits
no manifest. Use `extra-files` to point it at whatever holds the
version instead.
2. `extra-files`, for a version string release-please does not know
about: a CMake project() call, build.zig.zon, a Dockerfile LABEL.
Mark the line in the file with a comment:
set(PROJECT_VERSION 1.2.3) # x-release-please-version
3. `bump-minor-pre-major`. True while below 1.0.0, so a breaking change
bumps 0.3.x to 0.4.0 rather than to 1.0.0. Remove it at 1.0.0.
GO AND MAJOR VERSIONS
For v2 and later, Go requires the module path itself to gain a /v2
suffix. release-please will tag v2.0.0 but will not edit go.mod, so that
one is a manual step. The same applies to the import paths in every
file, which is why a Go v2 is a deliberate project rather than a merge.
The changelog sections. A type with `hidden: true` still counts
towards the version bump but does not appear in the changelog, which
is what keeps a hundred Dependabot commits out of the release notes.
Keep this list in step with pr-title.yml's `task_types`, or a title
that passes the check can produce a commit release-please ignores.
